descriptionChirho: Substantive adjective used as a noun meaning 'enemy', 'foe', or 'hostile person', referring to personal, national, or spiritual adversaries. The plural forms (AMP, NMP, GMP, 21x) and singular forms (AMS, NMS, GMS, VMS, 11x) represent the same lexical meaning with only grammatical number difference. Multilingual evidence is entirely consistent: Spanish 'enemigos/enemigo' (pl/sg), Hindi 'शत्रुओं–को/शत्रु' (shatrūon = enemies, shatru = enemy), Arabic 'أَعداءَ/أَعْدَاءَكَ' (a'dā' = enemies, pl) and 'عَدُوُّ/عَدوًّا' ('aduww = enemy, sg), Korean '원수들을/원수들이' (wonsudeur = enemies) and '원수가/원수인' (wonsu = enemy), Swahili 'adui' (enemy, same form sg/pl). The word covers enemies of God, of Christ, of believers, and personal foes (as in 'love your enemies').
